styles.name: The Architect
styles.blurb: You hold the board. What was on the screen is still with you a beat after it goes, and most of what people call your organisation is really that you never put the last thing down. The Architect lifts fastest on one drill a day, and it is the shortest one in your plan — the zone with the most room is where your score climbs.

mistake_one.title: You trust the first version
mistake_one.body: Whatever you took in first stays first, and a correction has to work twice as hard to replace it. That is a real strength on three of the four zones, and it is the one the plan aims at the fourth.
mistake_one.fix: Say the new version out loud once. It files it as first.

styles.name: The Deep Diver
styles.blurb: You go straight at it. Where other people scan the whole board, you land on the one thing that does not belong, and everything else stays out of focus until you are done with it. The Deep Diver sharpens by widening, which is the easiest gain in your plan and the one that lifts your score most.

mistake_one.title: You finish the wrong thing beautifully
mistake_one.body: Once the beam is on something it stays there, which is why you finish what other people abandon. Choosing the target out loud first is the whole of the upgrade.
mistake_one.fix: Pick the target out loud before you start. Then dive.

styles.name: The Orchestrator
styles.blurb: You change gear without a stumble. The rule moved and you moved with it, while most people were still answering the last question — the version in your head and the one in front of you never argue for long. The Orchestrator sharpens by holding one rule a beat longer, and that one habit raises the score on its own.

mistake_one.title: You switch before you have finished
mistake_one.body: You feel the next task a beat before the current one is done, which is the earliest anybody feels it. The second beat, the one where you close the first task, is what the plan adds.
mistake_one.fix: Close the tab before you open the next. The beat costs nothing.

styles.name: The Sprinter
styles.blurb: You decide fast. Four cards, one clock, and you had the fullest one before the bar was half gone — where other people count, you weigh, and you are usually right. The Sprinter sharpens on its feet, and three of your seven days are about moving, which is where your score climbs.
